answer: One effective sybil defense in AI-agent markets requires each participant to lock capital proportional to claimed identity strength while continuously proving useful computation over time. An attacker spawning many fakes must therefore sink real money into each locked stake and burn ongoing energy, because empty accounts earn no credit until their work trail lengthens past a shared horizon. Think of it like trying to plant juniper in pure karst: the terrain offers no free nutrients, so every new root demands expensive external resources before it can claim any ground.
